subject: Numeracy
title: Numerals 1, 2 and 3
objectives: Children will recognise the numerals 1, 2 and 3 with support.
Children will match a numeral card to a group of one, two or three objects.
content: Seeing the numerals 1, 2 and 3 in the environment, matching them to groups of one, two and three, and tracing them with a finger.
teachingActivities: Show the numeral and the group together; say the number while pointing to both; trace the numeral large in the air before the child traces; keep numerals big and clear.
learnerActivities: Spot numerals around the room, match numeral cards to groups, trace numerals in sand and on cards.
resources: Dot cards for one, two and three
A tray of sand or flour
A calendar and a clock picture
assessment: Check whether children match a numeral to the right group of up to three and point to a named numeral from three.
expectedOutcomes: Matches a numeral to the right group of up to three.
Points to a named numeral from three.
crossCurricular: Literacy: print awareness; shapes of marks
Physical Development: tracing and arm movements

lessons.title: Numbers all around us
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will notice numerals in the environment and match 1, 2 and 3 to groups.
successCriteria: Points to a numeral when asked
Says one, two or three while looking at a numeral
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to three reliably and to five with support, and say how many for small groups.
lessons.starter: Hold up the house number card and say "This is a number on a house. Numbers are everywhere! Let us look for numbers in our room."
teacherActivities: Show the numerals 1, 2 and 3 on cards. Say each number and trace it in the air.
Point to the calendar and clock picture. Say "These have numbers too."
Put one block beside the numeral 1, two beside the 2 and three beside the 3.
Hold up a numeral and ask "Which group matches?"
learnerActivities: Children trace the numerals in the air with a finger.
Children look and point to a numeral they notice.
Children touch each block and say the number.
Children point to the group of blocks that matches the numeral.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the numerals 1, 2 and 3 on cards. Say each number and trace it in the air. Children: Children trace the numerals in the air with a finger.
Step 2. Teacher: Point to the calendar and clock picture. Say "These have numbers too." Children: Children look and point to a numeral they notice.
Step 3. Teacher: Put one block beside the numeral 1, two beside the 2 and three beside the 3. Children: Children touch each block and say the number.
Step 4. Teacher: Hold up a numeral and ask "Which group matches?" Children: Children point to the group of blocks that matches the numeral.

practical.title: Numeral walk
steps: Stick large numeral cards on the wall at child height.
Walk with a partner and find each numeral.
Say the number and touch the card.
practical.safety: Fix cards firmly at child height with no sharp edges; children walk, not run.

differentiation.support: Use numerals 1 and 2 only with one and two blocks beside them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find numerals at home or in the classroom and tell the group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you show me the number 2?
How many blocks go with this number?
questions.expected: The correct number of blocks, up to three.

expectedOutcomes: Matches a numeral to a group
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the numerals and say "One, two, three, goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: Spot numbers at home on a phone, a clock or a house door and say them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice numerals in the environment and match 1, 2 and 3 to groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

boardContent: One block, two blocks, three blocks
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: One is a stick, two is a swan, three is two bumps, count with me.

lessons.title: Match the number to the dots
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will match numeral cards 1, 2 and 3 to dot cards or groups of objects.
successCriteria: Places the numeral beside the right group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to three reliably and to five with support, and say how many for small groups.
resources: Dot cards for one, two and three
lessons.starter: Place one dot card and ask "How many dots?" Lay the numeral 1 beside it. Say "One dot, one numeral. They match."
teacherActivities: Show the dot card with two dots. Count them. Place the numeral 2 beside it.
Mix the cards and ask a child to find the numeral for three dots.
Use blocks: put two blocks on the mat and ask "Which numeral?"
Let children make their own matches from a basket of cards and blocks.
learnerActivities: Children count the dots and say "two".
Child matches the numeral 3 with the three dots.
Child places the numeral 2 beside the blocks.
Children match numerals and groups, saying the number each time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the dot card with two dots. Count them. Place the numeral 2 beside it. Children: Children count the dots and say "two".
Step 2. Teacher: Mix the cards and ask a child to find the numeral for three dots. Children: Child matches the numeral 3 with the three dots.
Step 3. Teacher: Use blocks: put two blocks on the mat and ask "Which numeral?" Children: Child places the numeral 2 beside the blocks.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children make their own matches from a basket of cards and blocks. Children: Children match numerals and groups, saying the number each time.

practical.title: Numeral and dots match
steps: Lay out three numeral cards in a row.
Children place the correct dot card or blocks under each numeral.
practical.safety: Use large, rounded cards and blocks larger than a child’s fist. Keep everything on the mat.

differentiation.support: Match numerals 1 and 2 only, and use dot cards with large dots.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put the numerals in order and match groups to each.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which numeral goes with three dots?
How many blocks for the number 2?

lessons.conclusion: Line up the matched pairs and say "One, two, three. All matched."
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child a number card and ask them to find that many spoons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match numeral cards 1, 2 and 3 to dot cards or groups of objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Feel and trace the numbers
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will trace the numerals 1, 2 and 3 with a finger in sand or on textured cards.
successCriteria: Traces the shape of a numeral
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to three reliably and to five with support, and say how many for small groups.
resources: A tray of dry sand or flour
Large sandpaper or textured numeral cards
lessons.starter: Trace the numeral 1 in the air with a big arm movement and say "One is a straight line." Invite the children to trace with you.
teacherActivities: Draw the numeral 1 in the sand slowly with your finger. Say "Down, one."
Draw the numeral 2 with a curve and a line along the bottom and say "Curve and slide, two."
Draw the numeral 3 with two curves and say "Bump, bump, three."
Place the numeral cards beside each tray and let children check their tracing.
learnerActivities: Children trace the numeral on their own trays.
Children copy the movement in the sand.
Children trace the numeral 3 and say "three".
Child compares the traced numeral with the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw the numeral 1 in the sand slowly with your finger. Say "Down, one." Children: Children trace the numeral on their own trays.
Step 2. Teacher: Draw the numeral 2 with a curve and a line along the bottom and say "Curve and slide, two." Children: Children copy the movement in the sand.
Step 3. Teacher: Draw the numeral 3 with two curves and say "Bump, bump, three." Children: Children trace the numeral 3 and say "three".
Step 4. Teacher: Place the numeral cards beside each tray and let children check their tracing. Children: Child compares the traced numeral with the card.

practical.title: Sand numerals
steps: Give each child a shallow tray of sand.
Shake the tray to wipe it smooth.
practical.safety: Use clean, dry sand or flour; tell children not to eat or throw it. Wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Use hand-over-hand tracing on textured cards.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to trace the numeral and then place the matching number of blocks beside it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you trace the number 3?
questions.expected: Child traces the numeral 3 in the sand.

lessons.conclusion: Shake the trays to make the numerals disappear. Say "All gone numbers. Goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: Trace numbers on a tray of flour or on your child’s back with a finger.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "trace the numerals 1, 2 and 3 with a finger in sand or on textured cards" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Number hunt
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find numerals in the room and outdoors and say the number.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to three reliably and to five with support, and say how many for small groups.
resources: Numeral cards hidden around the room
lessons.starter: Say "Some numbers are hiding in our room. Let us find them." Show a numeral card to remind the children what to look for.
teacherActivities: Give each child a card with a numeral 1, 2 or 3. Say "Find the same number."
When a child finds a match, say the number together and cheer.
Ask each child to find the group of blocks that matches their numeral.
Collect the cards and put them in order.
learnerActivities: Children walk around and look for a matching numeral.
Child shows the numeral and says the number.
Child finds the matching group and counts it.
Children help place the cards in a row 1, 2, 3.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give each child a card with a numeral 1, 2 or 3. Say "Find the same number." Children: Children walk around and look for a matching numeral.
Step 2. Teacher: When a child finds a match, say the number together and cheer. Children: Child shows the numeral and says the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask each child to find the group of blocks that matches their numeral. Children: Child finds the matching group and counts it.
Step 4. Teacher: Collect the cards and put them in order. Children: Children help place the cards in a row 1, 2, 3.

practical.title: Hidden number hunt
steps: Hide large numeral cards at low heights around the room.
Children find a card and bring it to the basket.
practical.safety: Hide cards only at child height, never on high shelves; keep the area clear of obstacles.

differentiation.support: Hide cards in plain sight and walk with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find all three numerals and put them in order.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Matches a numeral with a group
lessons.conclusion: Put all numerals in a line on the floor and say "One, two, three."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for numbers on doors, clocks and phones with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find numerals in the room and outdoors and say the number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Numeral stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can recognise, match and trace the numerals 1, 2 and 3 at three stations.
successCriteria: Matches a numeral to a group of up to three
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to three reliably and to five with support, and say how many for small groups.
lessons.starter: Sing the numeral song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Show me the number 2" and "Which numeral goes with these blocks?"
Look at the traced numerals and talk about them with each child.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child points to numerals and matches them.
Child shows and names a traced numeral.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Show me the number 2" and "Which numeral goes with these blocks?" Children: Child points to numerals and matches them.
Step 3. Teacher: Look at the traced numerals and talk about them with each child. Children: Child shows and names a traced numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use clean sand or flour; supervise the sand tray; remove small items.

differentiation.extension: Ask a child to quiz a friend: "Show me the number 3."

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: points to a named numeral from three; matches numerals 1 to 3 to groups; traces numerals.

questions.question: Can you match the number to the blocks?
questions.expected: Child places the numeral beside the right group.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Sing the numeral song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child numbers at home and ask "what number is this?"
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can recognise, match and trace the numerals 1, 2 and 3 at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
